meta.name: Pocket Screen
meta.notes: Neutral iOS-like chrome; primary drives the lock-screen mesh wallpaper (with accent), the call/CTA buttons, app icons, live-activity card and tinted GET pills (text uses a darkened primary for contrast)

issues: Creativity 8: the lock-screen hero with live clock, frosted notification USPs and an incoming-call contact screen is a strong, coherent device metaphor. Typography 7: Urbanist 200 clock vs 700 titles works, but the mono eyebrows are overused. Layout 5, Polish 5, Brand robustness 8 (the mesh under a scrim handles both red and brown well), Mobile 5. Generic-template feel: low.
At scroll 0 the unlock timeline faded every widget (featured stack, note, stats, search) to opacity 0, so a large dead pink band sat directly under the lock screen on desktop, mobile and stress.
Only the home screen was counter-translated, not the footer, so a second empty band about one lock-screen tall opened between the contact list and the 'Instellingen' footer (very visible on mobile).
Mobile: the fixed demo badge sat on top of the 'Veeg omhoog om te openen' pill, and the lock content (3 notifications with 2-line text) pushed the pill below the fold.
Catalog: every result repeated its icon image as a big 16:10 'screenshot' box, which tripled the list length. It read as a product grid, not an App Store list.
Catalog segmented control was cut off hard at the right edge ('Kart onder…') with no hint that it scrolls.
Dock is a sticky element, so in full-page captures it appears mid-page on the catalog. This is a capture artefact and correct in a real viewport, so it was left alone.
fixed: Widgets now only drift and settle (y + scale) during the unlock instead of fading from 0. The part peeking out below the lock screen is real content, not a void. Icon rows still scale in from 0.85, staggered row by row.
The footer is translated together with the home screen in the ScrollTrigger timeline, which removes the gap between the contact and footer sections.

On mobile the badge moved to the top centre, where the camera island would be. The clock was tightened, notification text clamped to 1 line and lock padding reduced, so the pill and home bar fit on the first screen.
Catalog: only the top result keeps a large App Store-style 'screenshot' banner (brand-tinted mesh backdrop, drop-shadowed product). All other results are compact icon/name/GET rows.
Segmented control gets an edge fade mask, so the overflow reads as scrollable rather than broken.
